definitions.explanation: The day with the shortest period of daylight and the longest night of the year, occurring around December 21-22 in the Northern Hemisphere. In Japan, it is traditionally associated with eating kabocha squash and taking yuzu baths.

examples.japanese: {今年|ことし}の{冬至|とうじ}は12{月|がつ}22{日|にち}だ。
examples.english: This year's winter solstice is December 22nd.

examples.japanese: {冬至|とうじ}にはかぼちゃを{食|た}べる{習慣|しゅうかん}がある。
examples.english: There is a custom of eating kabocha squash on the winter solstice.

examples.japanese: {冬至|とうじ}を{過|す}ぎると、{少|すこ}しずつ{日|ひ}が{長|なが}くなっていく。
examples.english: After the winter solstice, the days gradually get longer.

notes:
The shortest day and longest night of the year, occurring around December 21-22 in Japan.

JAPANESE CUSTOMS:
- {柚子|ゆず}{湯|ゆ}: taking a bath with yuzu citrus fruit, believed to ward off illness
- かぼちゃ: eating kabocha squash for good health and good luck
- Traditionally, eating foods with "ん" in the name on this day brings luck

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {冬至|とうじ}の{日|ひ}: the day of the winter solstice
- {冬至|とうじ}を{迎|むか}える: to reach the winter solstice
- {冬至|とうじ}を{過|す}ぎる: to pass the winter solstice

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {夏至|げし}: summer solstice (longest day)
- {春分|しゅんぶん}: spring equinox
- {秋分|しゅうぶん}: autumn equinox
